newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-RAIN WASHES OUT TRIANGULAR FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-RAIN WASHES OUT TRIANGULAR FINAL.

text.p: South Africa and India will face up to each other again on Thursday after rain forced their final in the triangular series to be abandoned on Wednesday with the match delicately poised.
South Africa, chasing 192 to win, were 42 for one after 14.3 overs with an uncomfortable Gary Kirsten (20) and Jacques Kallis (eight) the not out batsmen.
Opener Andrew Hudson had been removed for seven after top-edging a pull off fast bowler Javagal Srinath.
If rain prevents a result on Thursday, the trophy for the tournament, which also included Zimbabwe, will be shared between South Africa and India.
Tight South African bowling and fielding -- and the needless run out of Mohammad Azharuddin for 60 -- had restricted India to 191 for nine from 50 overs after they won the toss and decided to bat.
A confident Azharuddin was run out in the 46th over, just as India were looking to accelerate, after batting partner Nayan Mongia failed to respond to his call for a comfortable single.
The Indian top order had also lost momentum after a brilliant catch by Jonty Rhodes removed Sachin Tendulkar for 32 just when the Indian captain was beginning to dominate the South African attack.
South African fast bowlers Allan Donald, with two for 23, and Lance Klusener, with two for 35, were the chief wicket-takers as a disciplined home team performance restricted the Indian batsmen.
